message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment.  
Here’s what you can do to get the most up‑to‑date information:

| Source | How to check |
|--------|--------------|
| **EPA AirNow** | Visit <https://www.airnow.gov/> and enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. It shows the current AQI, pollutant breakdowns, and health advisories. |
| **AirVisual / IQAir** | Go to <https://www.iqair.com/us/usa/california/los-angeles> (or the AirVisual app). They provide real‑time AQI, forecast, and historical trends. |
| **Local news sites** | Many local stations (e.g., KABC, KTLA) publish live air‑quality dashboards. |
| **Mobile apps** | Apps like *Plume Labs: Air Report*, *AQICN*, or *Weather Underground* give instant readings and alerts. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, you can also search “Los Angeles AQI” in Google; the search results often display the current AQI directly in the knowledge panel.

Let me know if you’d like help interpreting the AQI values or understanding what the numbers mean for health and outdoor activities!
